_what: The hand-kept half of the launch readiness report. readiness.py reads this and writes READINESS.md; nothing generated ever writes this file. Two lists: errors a person knows about, and how far each part of the site has been taken. Both exist because they cannot be measured off disk -- an error nobody has noticed is not in here, and no script can tell a first draft from a second.
_how_to_use: Add an error the moment it is found, with status open. When it is fixed, set status to fixed, put the commit in fixed_by, and name the preflight check that now guards it -- or say none, which is itself worth seeing. Move a feature to draft 2 only after it has actually been gone over, not after it has been touched.
_status_values: error.status: open | fixed | source_gap. feature.draft: 1 | 2 | unreviewed.

errors.what: At least one polling-place row has combined two municipalities: Atkinson & Gilmanton Academy Grant reads 'Errol Townhall 33 Dumont St', which is Errol's building with Colebrook's street and ZIP. This is the dangerous kind -- clean, plausible text naming a real building in the wrong town. RESOLVED 21 September: the row now reads 'Errol Town Hall 33 Main St At.& Gil. Ac. Gt. 03579' -- Errol's own street and ZIP rather than Colebrook's, so the bleed is gone and the row is internally consistent. NOT verified against any source that the Academy Grant's voters really do vote at Errol; unincorporated places commonly vote in a neighbouring town, so this is plausible and unconfirmed.

24 current-term bills where bill_text.json's version disagrees with the database's newest printing, two of them showing a fiscal note where the database holds the introduced bill. MEASURED 22 September, and 22 of the 24 were not an error at all. The comparison behind the number ranked a bill's printings by DocumentVersion.SortOrder, which is a stage order and not a chronological one -- 'As Amended by the House (2nd committee)' is 50 and 'As Amended by the Senate' is 30, though a House bill reaches the Senate later -- and it set the document's own printed heading against the database's separate vocabulary, which spells the same thing differently. Compared on the text instead, all 24 publish the right words: 23 are word-identical to the newest printing once the document heading is discounted and one differs by 13 words. The two fiscal-note ones were real and are fixed -- the text was the introduced bill both times and only the label was wrong, which is the worse way round.
errors.guard: a bill's version is read from its own heading, not its fiscal note

errors.what: town_officials.json is an NHDOT administrative contact directory dated 2 September 2025, not an elected-officials roster. It predates the November 2025 city elections and the March 2026 town elections, and carries about twelve town clerks across 234 municipalities and no tax collectors, treasurers or moderators at all.

Nothing schedules the nightly or the fetch lane. None of this machine's scheduled tasks names the repository, nightly.py or the lane, and there is no startup entry either, so every night that ran was started by hand. The gaps in the nightly log are not flaky automation; there is no automation. Deferred deliberately: the person wants this solved by moving the scheduled work to the cloud rather than by adding a Windows task, and after the current round of revisions.
errors.where: the fourth launch condition -- running unattended for a week
errors.guard: readiness.py now asks the task scheduler directly and says so, so this cannot be mistaken for flaky automation again

errors.what: The Secretary of State publishes no polling place for about a third of rows and prints 'If the polling location is blank contact your city/town clerk'. This is a hole in the source, not in the collection, but a reader still cannot find where to vote.

682 words of statute were deleted outright from five bills -- HB2, HB1606, SB127, SB193 and SB551. fetch_bill_text lists the General Court's page furniture so a bill can be told apart from a menu, and strip_chrome dropped any LINE containing one of those phrases; a bill's body is rendered a paragraph to a line. 'other resources' is a menu heading on their site and also ordinary English, and it cut 9 lines across the 2,234 cached pages of this term, every one of them the bill's own words and not one of them furniture. HB1606 lost the definition of 'real property', and the published page then used the term 26 times without ever defining it.
errors.where: a bill's Bill Text tab -- the text of the bill itself
errors.reported_by: found while measuring the registered 24-bill error, which turned out not to be one
errors.guard: stripping the page furniture never deletes a line of the bill
